title: SLO weekly ops standup template + risk heatmap
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight, repeatable template for weekly SLO-focused operations standups plus an embedded risk heatmap. Goal is to give cross-functional partners (product, serving-runtime, platform-engineering, support) a fast pulse on rollout status, regression signals, unresolved risks, and concrete owner actions for the coming week. Keep each meeting to 25 minutes.

Audience:
- Service owners and feature PMs with active SLO rollouts
- SREs and platform oncall
- Release engineers and QA leads
- Solutions engineering for customer-impacted rollouts

Cadence & logistics:
- When: Weekly, Wednesdays 10:30–10:55 PT
- Duration: 25 minutes strict
- Channel: ops-slo-standup Zoom + #ops-slo Slack summary thread
- Pre-reads required: 1) Latest SLO signal dashboard link, 2) Release notes for any model variant changes

Meeting Agenda (25 min):
1) Quick scoreboard (5 min)
   - Global SLOs: current 7d / 30d breach status (owner: SRE presenter)
   - Top 3 customer impact alerts in past 7 days (owner: support lead)

2) Rollout status & blockers (8 min)
   - Active rollouts (name, percentage traffic, target date, owner) — 1 min per rollout
   - Blockers and mitigation options — state explicitly: P0/P1, mitigation ETA, decision needed (owner: rollout lead)

3) Risk heatmap review (6 min)
   - Review top 5 risks from heatmap (see table below). Each risk: likelihood, impact, current mitigation, owner.
   - Decide one escalation or de-risking action for highest-rated risk.

4) Action items and follow-ups (4 min)
   - Confirm owners and due dates for all actions
   - Publish short Slack summary with actions and dashboard links

Standup template (copy into meeting doc):
- Date:
- Hosts: (SRE, PM)
- Scoreboard snapshot:
  • Service-level SLOs: [link to dashboard]
  • Error budget remaining (7d / 30d):
  • Recent regressions: short bullets and ticket refs
- Active rollouts:
  • Rollout A — 45% traffic — Target: 2026-06-10 — Owner: Rosa Martinez — Blocker: canary latency spike above target at 2kRPS — Mitigation: pause + revert script ready (JIRA-1234)
  • Rollout B — 10% traffic — Target: 2026-06-24 — Owner: Ethan Brooks — Blocker: model artifact signing delay — Mitigation: temp fallback image
- Top alerts this week:
  • Alert X — impact: partial failures on embeddings endpoints — ticket: JIRA-1302 — Owner: Liam Nguyen
- Action items (owner, due):
  • Action 1 — Owner — Due date — Status
  • Action 2 — Owner — Due date — Status

Risk heatmap (format for each risk):
- ID: R1
  Title: Latency regression under sustained burst (95th P95 increase)
  Likelihood: Medium
  Impact: High (customer timeouts, error budget burn)
  Current mitigations: autoscale policy, prefix cache warmup, canary throttling
  Next action: Add short-window load test and confirm autoscale thresholds (Owner: platform-eng — due 2026-06-07)

- ID: R2
  Title: Fallback model variant mismatch (semantic drift between primary and fallback)
  Likelihood: Low
  Impact: Medium
  Current mitigations: eval set gating, A/B sample checks
  Next action: Create rolling eval job and add alert on semantic spike (Owner: applied-ml — due 2026-06-14)

- ID: R3
  Title: Observability gaps for cold-start KV cache faults
  Likelihood: High
  Impact: Medium
  Current mitigations: synthetic KV tests are running but sparse
  Next action: Instrument cache fill time metric and add a dedicated dashboard panel (Owner: observability — due 2026-06-09)

- ID: R4
  Title: Release gating delay due to security sign-off backlog
  Likelihood: Medium
  Impact: Low (delays only)
  Current mitigations: pre-approved checklist for low-risk rollouts
  Next action: Work with security to create escrow sign-off path for routine infra changes (Owner: security-and-compliance — due 2026-06-21)

- ID: R5
  Title: Capacity contention in Dedicated pools during double-burst windows
  Likelihood: Low
  Impact: High (throttled customer jobs)
  Current mitigations: reserved burst margin, costed overflow to hosted API
  Next action: Simulate overlapping bursts and verify autoscale policies (Owner: dedicated — due 2026-06-15)

Decision log (short template):
- Date: 2026-06-02
- Decision: Pause Rollout A and run 1-hour controlled load test; revert if P95 > 800ms
- Rationale: observed 20% increase in P95 under synthetic 2kRPS test
- Owner: Rosa Martinez
- Follow-up ticket: JIRA-1234

Cross-team dependency tracker (short):
- Dependency: Observability instrumentation for KV cache metrics — Dep type: required — Owner: observability — Status: blocked by infra change (PR #58)
- Dependency: Security sign-off queue for model artifacts — Dep type: optional gating — Owner: security-and-compliance — Status: needs SLA

On-call escalation matrix (condensed):
- P0 (service unavailable): Notify SRE oncall -> Platform pager -> Exec notification if >30m
- P1 (partial outage / severe degradation): Notify feature SRE -> Platform rotation -> PM & support informed
- P2 (degradation with workaround): Triage in next standup, track in Slack thread

Unresolved questions (notes to self / TBD):
- Should we move standup cadence to twice-weekly during major multi-rollout periods? Pros/cons list needed.
- Do we standardize a single canary threshold across all services or allow per-service tuning?
- Is the current error-budget calculation suitable for model-generated variability, or do we need an adjusted metric for stochastic outputs?

Notes / scratchpad (quick capture):
- Quick command list to include in meeting notes: link to canary dashboard, link to rollback script, link to synthetic test runner, instructions to escalate to Platform Eng oncall.
- Remind PMs to attach a short one-line user impact summary to each rollout card.
- Keep meeting to 25 min — we lose value when it turns into deep technical debugging; move debugging to follow-up breakout.

How to use this template:
- Copy the standup template into the weekly meeting doc, populate scoreboard and rollouts before meeting (owners accountable).
- Update the risk heatmap row statuses during the meeting and publish a 1-paragraph summary to #ops-slo within 1 hour of the meeting end.
- Track actions in JIRA and reference ticket IDs in the meeting notes.

Appendix: quick checklist for rollout owner before a standup:
- Confirm canary telemetry is live and includes P50/P95/P99, error rate, and latency distributions
- Attach recent eval results for semantic drift if a model change is included
- List fallback variants and validation status
- Add a short mitigation plan for the top 2 identified risks

Draft/ToDo for this doc:
- Add small visual ASCII heatmap for quick scan (todo: create generator script)
- Link templates for synthetic load jobs and canary scripts
- Get buy-in from product and security on the escrow sign-off path

End of template.
